items.q: Anisocoria worse in dark with mild ptosis and anhidrosis localises to which pathway?
items.exp: Dilator failure shows in darkness with dilation lag; sweating pattern and pharmacology (cocaine, hydroxyamphetamine) localise central to postganglionic while imaging hunts dissection or Pancoast.
items.kp: Small pupil in dark with dry cheek: Horner.

items.q: Swinging flashlight test showing paradoxical dilation indicates what?
o: Relative afferent pupillary defect from optic nerve or severe retinal disease
items.exp: Asymmetric conduction delays consensual drive; neuritis, ischaemia, detachment and advanced glaucoma cause while media opacities never do. Filters grade depth.
items.kp: Pupil opening on light swing: afferent fault.

items.q: Painful Horner syndrome after neck trauma with neck pain needs which urgent step?
o: Carotid dissection imaging (CTA or MRA neck)
items.exp: Mural haematoma threatens stroke within days; antithrombotic with endovascular debates follows while Horner itself observes. Painless isolated cases still image routinely.
items.kp: Neck hurt, Horner new: scan carotid.

items.q: Painful pupil involving third nerve palsy with down and out eye mandates exclusion of what?
o: Posterior communicating artery aneurysm with urgent vascular imaging
items.exp: Compressive lesions strike superficial pupillary fibres first; CTA or MRA with neurosurgery precedes rupture while pupil sparing ischaemic palsies observe with vascular control.
items.kp: Blown pupil, eye down and out: aneurysm.

items.q: Pupil sparing complete third nerve palsy in elderly diabetic is managed how?
o: Microvascular ischaemia observing with vascular risk control
items.exp: Vasa nervorum ischaemia spares peripheral pupillary fibres; recovery over months expected while any pupil involvement or progression images urgently.
r: Correct. Ischaemic, watch and control risks.
items.kp: Spared pupil in diabetic third nerve: ischaemia watches.

items.q: Young woman with large regular pupil reacting poorly to light but tonically to near with absent ankle jerks has what?
o: Holmes Adie syndrome (tonic pupil) with denervation supersensitivity
items.exp: Ciliary ganglion denervation supersensitises sphincter to dilute pilocarpine with slow redilatation; benign course with reading glasses while deep tendon loss completes Holmes Adie.
r: Incorrect. AR pupils are small irregular.
items.kp: Big pupil slow to redilate plus lost jerks: Adie.

items.q: Small irregular pupils reacting to accommodation but not light with tabes dorsalis is which classic sign?
items.exp: Midbrain rostral lesions spare near fibres; penicillin treats with serology while pupils persist as scars. Bilaterality with irregularity distinguishes Adie.
r: Incorrect. Adie is large and regular.
items.kp: Near but not light, small irregular: neurosyphilis.

items.q: Cocaine versus hydroxyamphetamine drops in Horner localise lesions how?
o: Cocaine confirms Horner (no dilation); hydroxyamphetamine dilates only preganglionic lesions with intact terminals
items.exp: Cocaine blocks reuptake needing endogenous noradrenaline; hydroxyamphetamine releases stores present only when third order neurone survives, separating carotid (post) from Pancoast (pre).
items.kp: Cocaine proves Horner, hydroxyamphetamine places it.

items.q: Light near dissociation with upgaze palsy and convergence retraction nystagmus localises where?
o: Dorsal midbrain (Parinaud syndrome from pineal tumours)
items.exp: Pretectal compression blocks light while near fibres pass ventrally; pineal germinoma with hydrocephalus images urgently while lid retraction (Collier sign) companions.
items.kp: Cannot look up, pupils ignore light: pineal pressing.

items.q: Tadpole pupil with segmental iris sphincter spasm in young women is what and managed how?
o: Episodic segmental denervation supersensitivity; benign reassurance
items.exp: Denervated segments twitch into teardrop distortion briefly; Adie spectrum reassures while angle closure instead pains with high pressure.
items.kp: Brief teardrop pupil in youth: benign twitch.
